1.title: 3D Taylor–Green vortex
1.explore: Change grid size, backend and target iterations. Inspect velocity decay.
1.limits: Reference units. Use this small case to check installation and backend selection.

2.title: 2D Taylor–Green vortex
2.explore: Change grid size and target iterations. Compare the same physical time.
2.limits: Reference units. This is a planar numerical benchmark.

3.title: Taylor–Green vortex / TRT
3.explore: Compare the TRT collision model with example 02 at matching settings.
3.limits: Reference units. Collision models can have different stability limits.

4.title: 2D vortex / Smagorinsky
4.explore: Change grid resolution and compare decay with example 02.
4.limits: Reference units. Subgrid modelling does not replace a grid study.

5.title: 3D vortex / Smagorinsky
5.explore: Compare this 3D case with example 01 at matching settings.
5.limits: Reference units. Begin with a small grid and increase it gradually.

6.title: Driven cavity
6.explore: Run the cavity and inspect the recirculation pattern.
6.limits: Reference units. Wall-adjacent fields require grid refinement.

7.title: Forced channel flow
7.explore: Inspect the velocity profile across the channel.
7.limits: Reference units. Compare profiles after the flow has settled.

8.title: Wind around a block
8.explore: Edit domain, closed mesh, grid spacing and physics. Inspect slice and flow lines.
8.limits: Geometry uses metres. Demonstration viscosity is not atmospheric air.

10.title: Responsive hull search
10.explore: Enable evaluation and Run search. Pause holds the current candidate; disabling cancels. Hull geometry is an editable assembly of native GH expressions, points, mesh faces, volume measurement and transforms. Replace it with your own mesh; no Hawa hull node is required.
10.limits: Single fluid, submerged hull. No waves or buoyancy. Short scores demonstrate search; they do not establish an optimum.

11.title: 3D field visualization
11.explore: Use the shared snapshot to compare planes, tubes, contours and isosurfaces. Change field and colour map.
11.limits: Use one snapshot for comparisons. Keep colour ranges fixed when comparing cases.

12.title: Local airfoil and RC wing
12.explore: Choose an offline NACA code or local coordinate file. Edit wing span/chord. Load your own local polar.
12.limits: The bundled polar is synthetic format data. Lifting-line results assume attached flow; stall is not predicted.

13.title: Record and replay
13.explore: Choose a new absolute output directory. Start Record, wait for completion, then change Frame.
13.limits: Recording creates files. Use a new directory for each run. Playback must use the returned manifest.

14.title: Stationary curved sphere
14.explore: Run the sphere. Inspect pressure and surface samples; compare grid spacings.
14.limits: Experimental stationary curved links. Do not combine with refinement or moving bodies.

15.title: Fixed refinement patch
15.explore: Edit the domain and interior patch; run both grids and compare their field planes.
15.limits: One fixed 2:1 BGK patch. Keep interpolation stencils in fluid. No automatic adaptive mesh.

16.title: Cylinder wake recording
16.explore: Set a new absolute directory, then record the wake. Pause/resume or cancel. Replay saved frames.
16.limits: The full recording runs 8000 steps. Use a smaller trial first. Outlet and domain size affect the wake.

17.title: Oscillating cylinder
17.explore: Set travel amplitude in metres. Run the case; inspect the shared field snapshot and moved body.
17.limits: Prescribed motion, uniform BGK. Keep the full trajectory two cells from domain faces. Check grids and cycle averages.

18.title: Pitching airfoil
18.explore: Edit the offline NACA section and wing. Set pitch amplitude in radians; run and inspect loads.
18.limits: Coarse thick-foil demonstration. RC boundary layers are not resolved. Motion does not respond to fluid forces.

19.title: Rotating paddle
19.explore: Set RPM and run. Inspect body pose, torque and signed fluid power.
19.limits: Single fluid. No water surface, cavitation or free-body response. This is not a validated propeller model.

20.title: Completed-cycle motion search
20.explore: Run search. Each amplitude is evaluated only after settling and complete measured cycles. Pause or cancel as needed.
20.limits: Default objective is input power. Compare longer settling, more cycles and finer grids before ranking designs.
